    • depositExtractAndPlacement

      public static void depositExtractAndPlacement(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> factory, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback)
      To reproduce: modifier-deposit four dirt into Storage, release the modifier and plain-click with an empty hand; the four dirt return to the hand. Store ten stone and plain-click it holding 60 stone: the hand fills to 64, six stone stay stored, and nothing drops. Then modifier-click the top of an ordinary block holding two dirt; a Storage Stack holding the two dirt appears there and the hand is empty.

    • disabledTypesRefuseNewBlocksButKeepExistingOnes

      public static void disabledTypesRefuseNewBlocksButKeepExistingOnes(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer messagePlayer, List<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> messages, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      To reproduce, for each stack type in turn: have an admin disable it (for example enable_singles_stack_block = false) with max_pile_height at least 2, and reload. Select that type and modifier-click the top of a stone block holding an item it accepts: no block appears, the item stays in hand, and the hotbar says that type's placement is disabled. An existing block of that type keeps working: modifier-click its side to deposit one item, then release the modifier and plain-click it empty-handed to take the item back. Fill another existing block and modifier-click its top (for Storage, also its side): it does not grow and the hand keeps its items. A hopper feeding a third full block does not grow it either. Re-enable the type: the same placement, top click, and hopper each add a block.

    • maximumHeightRefusesGrowthAndHidesHeadroom

      public static void maximumHeightRefusesGrowthAndHidesHeadroom(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> factory, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      To reproduce, for each stack type and for max_pile_height 1 and then 2: build a column of that many full blocks of the type and point a hopper at it; the hopper adds nothing. Select that type and modifier-click the column's top holding an item it accepts: nothing grows and the item stays in hand. Raise max_pile_height by one and reload: the hopper grows the column by one block. The advertised slot counts (only the column's own blocks at the cap, one more block of headroom below it) need a slot-addressing automation probe to see.

    • deniedItemsRefuseDepositsAndOnlyModDenialStopsAutomation

      public static void deniedItemsRefuseDepositsAndOnlyModDenialStopsAutomation(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer messagePlayer, List<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> messages, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      To reproduce: add minecraft:dirt to disable_items and reload. Select Storage and modifier-click a Storage Stack holding dirt: nothing moves, the dirt stays in hand, and the hotbar names the disabled item. Modifier-clicking the top of a stone block with that dirt places nothing. The same click holding stone deposits it, and a hopper feeding dirt into the stack still works. Now clear disable_items and add minecraft to disable_mods instead: the dirt deposit is refused with the disabled-mod message and the hopper adds nothing more, but a plain click still takes stored items out. Clear disable_mods and the dirt deposit works.

    • blockUseDenialFreezesStackGestures

      public static void blockUseDenialFreezesStackGestures(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> factory, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback, BiConsumer<net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer,net.minecraft.core.BlockPos> denyBlockUse, Runnable allowBlockUse)
      To reproduce: stand in a claim you are not trusted in, or anywhere a protection mod denies you block interaction, beside a Storage Stack holding three stone and a Singles Stack holding one item. V-deposit a stick into the Storage Stack; plain-click it empty-handed; select Toggle Permanent and sneak-modifier-click it empty-handed; sneak-click it with a redstone torch; sneak-click the Singles item with a soul torch. Nothing about either stack changes, and the stick and the empty hand stay as they were. Switch to Spectator mode outside the claim and repeat: again nothing changes. Back in Survival outside the claim, all five apply.

      The torch steps assert the stacks, not the hand: a loader may let a held item act as an ordinary item when only block use is denied (Forge's setUseBlock(DENY) leaves the torch free to be placed beside the stack).

    • stateAndLogout

      public static void stateAndLogout(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> factory, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback)
      No in-game form: the client keeps its selected mode across connections and re-sends its state with the first click after reconnecting, so a player sees no difference. It guards that the server records the mode and modifier a gesture-state packet reports, and that logout removes that per-player record so the server falls back to Storage mode with the modifier released.

    • successfulUseEmitsBlockChange

      public static void successfulUseEmitsBlockChange(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack,net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer> factory, InteractionChecks.LoaderClick callback)
      To reproduce: put a sculk sensor beside a Storage, a Singles, and a Bar Stack. Deposit into and extract from Storage, toggle its permanence, and rotate it with a redstone torch; rotate a Singles item with a soul torch. Each successful use vibrates. Extract one of two Singles items or bars, then the last: the first vibrates as a change, the last only as the block's destruction.
